text.p: Lufthansa Cargo saw a 2.2 percent fall in average yields in 1996, Deutsche Lufthansa AG chief financial officer Klaus Schlede said.
Schlede was outlining the trends behind the cargo unit's 59.8 million mark 1996 loss at a Frankfurt news conference.

"Our cargo carrier suffered in 1996 from the weak growth of the air freight markets in Japan, India and some European countries but also from the fact that high excess capacity in the market led to sharp falls in prices and yields," he said.
Schlede noted that Lufthansa Cargo was also burdened last year with extra fuel charges amounting to $35 million.

The cargo airline's main traffic revenue growth markets last year were Europe (up 9.9 percent), the U.S. (7.6 percent), the Middle East (up 9.4 percent) and Central and South America (up 2.7 percent).
But Asia/Pacific traffic revenue fell 0.6 percent, Germany declined three percent and Africa slumped 15.4 percent.
